chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: Recording with Billie Holiday: the big-band dates and Aladdin session
summary: He did several records with Billie, mostly big-band dates where he faked the reading, and recalls Detour Ahead.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Getting back to Billie Holiday a little bit -- you did make a couple of recordings with Billie --
Was there one with a big band.

All of 'em was with big bands and violins and these guys had all this music. They opened up a sheet of music man about 3 feet long. And, I didn't know nothin' about no music, but I didn't say anything, so. By the time they got through rehearsing, I had my part down, see. I just listened. Some thing happened in Germany ---- Any time any music was available that I had to be playing in big bands and things, I just listened. And then when I found out I couldn't do it I just turned the volume down, and be strummin' -- I escaped out of more traps and things.
Do you remember making a recording with Billie and Bill Taylor on bass, Joe Guy on trumpet, Bill Springer in '46 and
No I don't even remember -- Billy Taylor on bass? . . .
Were there other records that you remember making with Billie?
Yeah, I made "Good Morning Heartache," and "What is this thing called love," I think I have about 8 bars maybe on that. But otherwise you can hardly hear me on those.

How about the date in April of '51 -- The record was released as "Lady Day with Tiny Grimes Sextet." Do you remember those? "Be fair to Me," Rocky Mountain Blues, "Blue Turning Grey over you," "Detour Ahead". It was on Aladdin Records.
"Detour Ahead," I remember that ... I can't remember too much. I remember it, but its very faint. 'Cause I remember "Detour Ahead" -- that was a tough tune. I'd like to get some of those things.
Heywood Henry was on saxophone on one of the numbers...
I think he musta played baritone, I think. . . .
Its funny -- these things you've made and forgot all about em. They were just gigs, you know.
Did you know Billie Holiday well?
